questions.question_text: Two positive numbers have a sum of $18$. One of them is $x$. Which expression gives their product $P$ as a function of $x$?

options.why: Rearranged the constraint as $y = x - 18$ instead of $y = 18 - x$.
Subtracted $x^{2}$ from the sum instead of multiplying $x$ by $18 - x$.
Used $y = 18 + x$, adding $x$ to the sum instead of subtracting it.

questions.solution_text:
Let the numbers be $x$ and $y$.
$x + y = 18$
$y = 18 - x$
$P = xy$
$= x(18 - x)$
$= 18x - x^{2}$

questions.question_text: A rectangular picture frame is made from $52$ cm of moulding. The frame is $x$ cm long. Which expression gives the enclosed area $A$ cm$^{2}$ as a function of $x$?

options.why: Used $y = 52 - x$, treating the whole perimeter as one length plus one width.
Halved only the $y$ term of $2x + 2y = 52$, giving $y = 26 - 2x$.
Used $y = 52 - 2x$, subtracting both widths from the whole perimeter.

questions.question_text: A rectangular label must have an area of $84$ cm$^{2}$. Its width is $x$ cm. Which expression gives the perimeter $P$ cm as a function of $x$?

options.why: Doubled the width but not the length when adding up the four sides.
Doubled the length but not the width when adding up the four sides.
Added one width and one length only, giving half the perimeter.
Subtracted only one square from each side length instead of two.
Used the full width $2x$ of the cut as the height instead of $x$.
Used $2x$ as the height and subtracted only one square from each side length.

questions.solution_text:
Cutting $x$ from both ends of each side leaves a base of $(16 - 2x)$ cm by $(10 - 2x)$ cm.
The folded-up height is $x$ cm.
$V = x(16 - 2x)(10 - 2x)$

questions.question_text: A closed cylindrical tin has a volume of $800$ cm$^{3}$, base radius $r$ cm and height $h$ cm. Which expression gives the total surface area $S$ cm$^{2}$ as a function of $r$?

options.why: Counted only one circular end instead of both.
Wrote the curved surface as $\pi r h$ instead of $2\pi r h$.
Counted one end only and used $\pi r h$ for the curved surface.
Inverted the similar-triangle ratio, using $\dfrac{20}{15}$ in place of $\dfrac{15}{20}$.
Applied the triangle area formula $\tfrac{1}{2}bh$ to a rectangle.
Inverted the ratio and also halved, treating the rectangle as a triangle.

questions.solution_text:
Let the height of the rectangle be $y$ cm.
The triangle above the rectangle is similar to the whole triangle.
$\dfrac{y}{15} = \dfrac{20 - x}{20}$
$y = 15 - \dfrac{3x}{4}$
$A = xy$
$= x\left(15 - \dfrac{3x}{4}\right)$
$= 15x - \dfrac{3x^{2}}{4}$

questions.question_text: For a cylinder, the sum of the base radius $r$ cm and the height $h$ cm is $21$ cm. What is the domain of $r$ in this model?

options.why: Halved the total, as if the constraint were a perimeter with two of each length.
Imposed positivity only, ignoring that $h = 21 - r$ must also be positive.
Doubled the total instead of using it directly as the cap.

questions.solution_text:
$r + h = 21$, so $h = 21 - r$.
A radius must be positive, so $r > 0$.
A height must be positive, so $21 - r > 0$.
$r < 21$
The domain is $0 < r < 21$.

questions.question_text: A rectangle is inscribed in a semicircle of radius $10$ cm with one side along the diameter. The rectangle has width $2x$ cm. Which expression gives its area $A$ cm$^{2}$ as a function of $x$?

options.why: Used $x$ as the full width of the rectangle instead of $2x$.
Substituted the full width $2x$ into Pythagoras' theorem instead of the half-width $x$.
Used $x$ as the width but $2x$ inside Pythagoras' theorem, mixing the two.

questions.solution_text:
The top corner is $x$ cm horizontally from the centre, on a circle of radius $10$ cm.
Let the height be $y$ cm.
$x^{2} + y^{2} = 100$
$y = \sqrt{100 - x^{2}}$
$A = 2x \times y$
$= 2x\sqrt{100 - x^{2}}$

questions.question_text: A closed box has a square base of side $x$ cm and a total surface area of $150$ cm$^{2}$, so its height is $h = \dfrac{150 - 2x^{2}}{4x}$. What is the domain of $x$?

options.why: Solved $2x^{2} < 150$ as $x < 75$, dividing by $2$ without taking a square root.
Ignored the factor $2$, solving $x^{2} < 150$ instead of $2x^{2} < 150$.
Used only the positive-length condition and never required $h > 0$.

questions.solution_text:
A side length must be positive, so $x > 0$.
The height must also be positive, so $150 - 2x^{2} > 0$.
$2x^{2} < 150$
$x^{2} < 75$
$x < \sqrt{75}$
$x < 5\sqrt{3}$
The domain is $0 < x < 5\sqrt{3}$.
